text:
ana: quick heads-up — after the runtime change yesterday (compile-time kernel selection tweak), we see a 12-18% p99 latency regression on some long-context chat workloads. traced a few runs with nsys and perfetto, looks like the hot path moved from fused-attn to an unexpected memcpy-heavy path.

mrinal: ugh. do we have before/after traces?

ana: attaching snippets below. ran on perfbox-12 with the same model and batch profile.

ana: nsys command I used:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace_after --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=none --cpuctx --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi
python run_inference.py --model rwd-open-64b --batch-profile small
```

ana: extract from the timeline (after-change):
```
CUDA Kernel: fused_attention_v2  duration=1.4ms  (used to be ~0.6ms)
cudaMemcpyAsync H2D              duration=0.9ms   (spike +0.7ms)
KVCache::write_kv_page          duration=1.1ms   (new hotspot)
```

ana: before-change trace (same host):
```
CUDA Kernel: fused_attention_v1  duration=0.65ms
KVCache::write_kv_page          duration=0.2ms
cudaMemcpyAsync H2D              duration=0.15ms
```

kaitlyn: interesting — sounds like kernel selector is picking a different attention kernel variant and that variant has a larger memory copy pattern. could be tiling / block config change.

mrinal: also possible the KV cache layout changed alignment, causing extra page writes. did any of the commit touches change buffer packing?

ana: looking at the commit range:
- commit a8f7d3c (runtime: prefer kernel variant v2 for seq_len>1024)
- commit b3c9faa (kv: change page allocator align to 256 bytes)
- commit c2e12ff (perf: minor launch config autotune)

ana: i ran a quick git-bisect locally and it points at b3c9faa (kv allocator). but need more traces to be sure — bisect on perf is noisy.

tomas: can you paste the bisect commands you used? i can run on CI perf pool.

ana: sure — this is what I ran:
```bash
git bisect start HEAD a1b2c3d
git bisect run ./perf/regression_test.sh --repro-args "--seq-length 2048 --batch 4"
```
perf/regression_test.sh returns exit code 0 if p99 <= baseline * 1.05 else 1.

ana: output snapshot from one failing try (on b3c9faa):
```
[RUN] seq=2048 batch=4
p50=24.3ms p95=68.1ms p99=104.5ms
baseline_p99=89.0ms
REGRESSION
```

kaitlyn: thanks. CI run would be good to confirm. I'll queue a job on perf-pool-3. Tomas, want me to include the nsys capture wrapper?

tomas: yes please — include pre/post kernel names and nvtx markers around KV write routines. also capture both `cudaMemcpy` and `memcpy` events.

ana: added NVTX markers in the test harness: `nvtxRangePushA("kv_write"); kv.write(...); nvtxRangePop();`

perf-bot: scheduled perf-pool-3 job #4529, runner: perfbox-3. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/traces/4529/

ci-bot: job #4529 started (commit b3c9faa).

perf-bot: nsys trace uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/traces/4529/trace_after.qdrep, perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/4529 (internal)

mrinal: grabbing the trace now. quick grep on the qdrep shows a 4x increase in `kv_write` NVTX spans and two big `cudaMemcpyAsync` spikes right before the new fused-attn launch.

mrinal: flamegraph snapshot (simplified):
```
fused_attention_v2 -> 35%
KVCache::write_kv_page -> 28%
cudaMemcpyAsync H2D -> 20%
other -> 17%
```

kaitlyn: that matches ana's local traces. strange that fused_attention_v2 is heavier but also there's more memcopies. maybe the v2 kernel needs a prepacked input buffer and we added an on-path conversion in the allocator change.

tomas: hypothesis: allocator align 256 bytes triggered a fallback path that does a host staging copy for unaligned buffers. we should check the allocator code path for `needs_staging()` or similar.

ana: grep shows `if (addr % 256 != 0) use_staging = true;` in allocator. that was the change. before we had 64-byte align so fewer buffers required staging.

mrinal: bingo. staging will cause extra memcpy H2D and a slower kernel launch prep. that explains both the memcpy spikes and the fused_attention duration increase (waiting for DMA).

kaitlyn: suggested fixes:
- revert alignment to 64 (quick test)
- or change allocator to prefer 64 but keep 256 for large contiguous allocations only
- add a fast-path that avoids staging when the HW supports unaligned DMA (check cuda attrs)

ana: i ran a quick revert locally (back to 64) — microbench on perfbox-12 shows p99 back to baseline within noise (~+1%).

tomas: can we do a smaller targeted change: only for KV cache pages that are going to be written by CPU path, keep 64. For pages allocated for compiled kernels' scratch, keep 256. PR incoming?

ana: i'll open a PR with the targeted allocator fix and include the before/after nsys traces and the bisect artifacts. PR will reference this thread and attach traces to the CI run.

mrinal: for the PR, include perfetto slices and the qdrep files, and a small regression test that runs `--seq-length 2048 --batch 4` and asserts p99 within 5% of baseline.

kaitlyn: also add a note to rollback the kernel selector change if we see any further regressions — while this bounce seems allocator-driven, kernel variants may interact.

perf-bot: CI perf job #4529 result: FAIL (p99 103.9ms vs baseline 89.0ms)

ci-bot: created issue #832 in perf-regressions with links to traces and bisect log.

tomas: thanks everyone. action items:
- ana: open PR with allocator fix + traces (ETA 2h)
- mrinal: add regtest harness for CI gating (ETA EOD)
- kaitlyn: prepare rollback playbook for kernel selector (ETA tomorrow)

ana: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2048 — includes qdrep + perfetto links and the bisect notes. cc @tomas @mrinal

mrinal: reviewing now. if tests good, let's get it onto the perf-pool canary and re-run the baseline comparison.

ana: once PR merges I'll kick off a canary run and post results here. thanks for the rapid triage :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: when uploading traces, please include the `cudaDeviceGetAttribute` dump (for checking unaligned DMA capability).

ana: noted, will include device attrs next trace.

kaitlyn: great thread — feel free to ping me if the canary shows any other weirdness.

ana: last note — we should add a short test in `perf/coverage` that asserts allocator alignment invariants so future refactors don't surprise us.

ci-bot: thread archived to perf-regressions channel reference.
